- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is high or trending up.
- Underestimate prices after sharp declines; model should anticipate mean reversion toward prior range, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes; if sentiment is low or flat, suppress forecast overshoots.
- When sentiment is consistently low or negative, model should favor downward bias, not follow recent highs.
- If true outcome shows early sharp drop after forecast peak, reduce forecast slope in subsequent days.
- For 30-day horizon, model should not ignore recent 7–14 day trend; if sentiment is weak, align forecast with 14-day moving average rather than 30-day trend.
- If sentiment is rising but price drops, model should not assume continuation; adjust downward bias to reflect sentiment divergence.
- Avoid forecasting above 10% above recent 14-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish and confirmed.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, forecast should not overshoot below 10% of recent low unless confirmed by technical indicators.
- When sentiment is volatile, model should not overfit to short-term sentiment swings; use sentiment as a filter, not a driver.
